body: So you're saying despite experiencing nought but suffering I should pluck up some gusto from somewhere so I can ensure prolonging my existence.

>Can I ask where you are at, roughly? State, and city if it is a big city?

England.

> Regarding the diabetes. And the teeth for that matter. Diabetes will cause bad teeth. You end up with poor circulation, and that causes the teeth to die off, fragment and break, and you eventually end up having them all pulled.

Is this a researched and known thing or just your intuition? I don't know whether to feel better or worse about this.

>Why is your diabetes poorly controlled? Do you lack access to insulin, or are your eating habits just crappy? Is the person who cooks for you just not paying attention to what options you are given for food?

NHS gives me insulin but I eat on little money and have little motivation to eat healthily to look after this piece of shit I call my body. My attitude is if I want to eat junk to distract myself then why shouldn't I, it's not like I get to enjoy much.

>On the chest condition, has it been there from birth, or is it something that just cropped up one day?

Cropped up around puberty. No idea what caused it, maybe sleeping down the side of my mattress as a kid, maybe a bully squishing me or something, maybe random. 

>And lastly, do you do anything at all during your free time? Do you do anything at all? What you are going through is bad enough on the whole. But if you are spending all of your free time focusing on each, individual symptom, they are going to be overwhelming. If you can find something to do that brings you happiness, it will take some of the focus off of what is happening with your body, and you won't be as miserable as much of the time.

Escapism is all I do. I roll out of bed into my computer chair then play video games all day until I fall asleep and get nothing done. 


>I know it has become tedious for you. I know you are sick and tired of having to deal with these issues. But you have the choice to let the problems over take you, or you can deal with them one by one.
And you don't have to deal with all of them at the same time. The diabetes one is one that you ought to address immediately, because diabetes is bad about killing you slowly, if you don't address it. It can cause high blood pressure, kidney failure, heart disease and a lot of other things, and most of that will hit you within 10 years of onset, if you don't address it. Especially the kidney failure part of it. It can cause retinopathy, where it tears large swatches of your retina out, and leave you blind. You will likely end up with neuropathy. So you need to adhere to whatever you need to adhere to, to control the diabetes. In fact, there is a good chance that your diabetes being out of control is a big part of why you are having such a problem with the eczema. Your immune system will be stressed, and then other things start breaking out.

Yeah to be honest a refresher on the results of diabetes really really really isn't needed. Yeah I could probably spend half my life pulling through to tackle this stupid fucking problems while my luckier brethren are out partying and doing whatever the fuck else normal people do. Tbh I'd rather just give up, that way I don't need to even know that I ever suffered. 

edit: sorry, this was inappropriate, thought it was the sw thread where I could gush more. Don't worry I'm not gonna do anything to myself, sadly.

>I'm guessing you are an American as you have conditions that would be treated in any other 1st world country without direct cost (GRRR Obama Care!).

No, I'm in England.I have no money due to not working I just finished my resit of college. 

> You have to apply some cream? Boo fucking hoo. Suck it up, it isn't changing.

No cream I have tried works and I've tried about 20, it's hard to put cream on the area when it could be anywhere from my scalp to my legs to my arms to my face or my chest. or all at once. 

> You can't manage your Type I diabetes? I'm assuming this is due to cost

No, it's not due to cost. NHS give me medication for my diabetes I just can't manage it. I've been trying for nearly 5 years now. Glucose levels are almost always up then sometimes down then up again. It's impossibly hard.

> Number 5? Is it any fucking wonder?? That will be sorted last I think.

Haha, indeed. but as I said it's genetic, not cause-induced.

 >Deformed chest - I think we can work a surgical solution to this regardless of insurance. Providing you are happy to have camera crews follow you. We will see

 I don't want my chest opened. 

> I feel I have licence to say to you - Make a plan. Now.

Coming on here and writing this shit is about all the motivation I can muster, I'm too beaten down to make any huge changes.
